text:
kat (Finance): Received invoice INV-5421 from ModelLab for $45,300 for "gpu-hours" dated 2025-09-12. Vendor says usage was on our dedicated pool. Did we actually allocate vendor jobs to Dedicated?
vendor-bot: Usage event: vendor=ModelLab, job_id=ml-vend-778, pool=dedicated-prod, start=2025-09-10T02:14Z, end=2025-09-11T18:00Z, charge=45300 USD. Link: https://billing.vendor/modelab/INV-5421
ryan (Eng-ML): We have a sandbox booking with ModelLab but they should be isolated to the `vendor-sandbox` pool. I didn't schedule anything on `dedicated-prod`.
nina (DedicatedOps): Checking router logs. Possible cause: pool aliasing rule for project:vendor-models used to map to vendor-sandbox, but a recent policy change added `project:legacy-models` to dedicated-prod whitelist. If ModelLab used legacy project creds, requests could've routed to dedicated.
olga (Legal): If vendor used the wrong project, contract clauses determine liability. We should collect evidence before rejecting invoice.
kat (Finance): Action: we should hold payment pending investigation. Can ops produce a mapping of job_ids -> project -> actual VM ids + timestamps? That will let us confirm the routing.
nina (DedicatedOps): Will run query: `SELECT job_id, project, pool, instance_id FROM infra.routing_logs WHERE job_id IN ('ml-vend-778') OR timestamp BETWEEN '2025-09-10' AND '2025-09-11'` Will attach CSV. ETA 2h.
ryan (Eng-ML): I'll check ModelLab job manifest and our vendor onboarding notes to see which project they used. If they used legacy creds, we can ask for vendor-side credit.
kat (Finance): Also need cost impact to internal committed capacity. If vendor actually consumed dedicated capacity, we may owe underprovision penalty to our cloud provider or impact other customers. Nina, include capacity utilization delta in the report.
nina (DedicatedOps): Noted. Preliminary: that week showed a 9% spike in dedicated utilization on cluster-a. Will include hourly breakdown.
vendor-bot: Vendor status: ModelLab support ticket opened by vendor at 2025-09-13T08:10Z ref=ML-TKT-210. They claim they launched against project `models-legacy` and expected sandbox mapping.
olga (Legal): Please preserve all logs. If vendor billing is in error, we'll ask ModelLab for a full credit and revised invoice. If not, we must allocate cost to the vendor account and process payment.
kat (Finance): Ok timeline: 1) nina provide CSV + capacity delta (due: 2h). 2) ryan validate vendor manifest and confirm project used (due: 4h). 3) legal to draft vendor dispute email if logs show misroute (olga) (due: EOD). Finance will hold payment until we have final determination.
ryan (Eng-ML): Found manifest snippet: `project: models-legacy`, `auth: service-account-legacy@models.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. That matches the legacy project tag. Could be our routing policy mistake.
nina (DedicatedOps): CSV uploaded: https://storage.redwood/finance/modelab-misroute-1769998888.csv total billed hours on dedicated-prod=156 GPU-hours, estimated cost attributed=45300. Capacity delta attached.
kat (Finance): Thanks. Olga, please prepare dispute and cc procurement. I'll mark invoice as disputed in AP and block payment.
olga (Legal): Drafted email ready. If ModelLab confirms they used legacy creds, we'll push for credit. Sending now.
vendor-bot: ModelLab response received: "We launched with legacy project creds; assumed sandbox mapping; requesting credit." Support ref=ML-TKT-210 update.
kat (Finance): Great. Closing loop: Finance will hold payment; ops will patch routing policy to remove legacy project from dedicated whitelist (nina). Nina, please add an e2e test so vendor sandbox mapping can't be bypassed.
nina (DedicatedOps): Will remove legacy-project whitelist and push test. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1342 ETA: 24h.
kat (Finance): Final note: once vendor issues credit, we'll re-run attribution and update committed capacity reconciliations. Thanks team.
